content.title: About
content.content: Papaya nectar is a sweet non‑alcoholic beverage made from ripe papaya, water, sugar, and sometimes preservative additives. It has a bright tropical aroma, a gentle orange‑red color, and a refreshing taste.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Papaya originates from Central and South America but is now cultivated in tropical regions worldwide.
Papaya contains 3–5 times more vitamin C than an orange.
The fruit contains the enzyme papain, which aids digestion.
Nectar is often used as a base for cocktails and dessert sauces.
In some cultures papaya is a symbol of hospitality and abundance.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system, promotes collagen synthesis, and acts as an antioxidant.

items.title: Contains vitamin A and carotenoids
items.content: Help maintain healthy vision and skin.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Papain enzyme helps break down proteins and reduces post‑meal heaviness.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potassium regulates fluid balance and supports heart function.

items.title: Low‑calorie drink
items.content: One cup (250 ml) provides about 80–100 kcal, making it a good alternative to sugary sodas.

items.title: Papaya allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to papaya or the papain enzyme.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Commercial nectars often contain added sugar, which may be unsuitable for diabetics or those watching weight.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Certain versions may include preservatives (e.g., potassium sorbate) that can cause sensitivity in susceptible people.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve papaya nectar chilled as a standalone drink, use it in smoothies, cocktails, dessert sauces, and marinades. It can be added to yogurt, oatmeal, or fruit salads to boost flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: After opening, keep the nectar refrigerated in a tightly sealed container for 5–7 days. Unopened product should be stored in a cool, dry place at up to 25 °C, respecting the expiration date on the package.
